items.title: The Gospels: Are They Historical?
items.description:

morning_soundtrack.snippet: In 2022, brakence broke through with hypochondriac , a bizarro hyperpop-rap whirlwind of an album. The 24-year-old artist is back today with "ready or noT," his first new music since then. It comes with an eccentric music video by fellow musician quadeca.

morning_soundtrack.title: Ween Announce Boognish Provides, 14-CD Box Set Of Previously Unreleased Chocolate And Cheese Tour Shows
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Ween are opening the vaults with Boognish Provides , a new collection of seven previously unreleased concerts from their 1994-95 Chocolate And Cheese tour. Arriving next month via Rhino, the 14-CD box set and condensed 2-LP edition capture the band at a pivotal moment, shortly after they began touring with a full backing band featuring bassist Andrew Weiss and drummer Claude Coleman.

morning_soundtrack.title: Remi Wolf – “I Won’t Cry”
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Palo Alto singer Remi Wolf started off as a kind of alt-pop artist, but she seems to be inching ever-closer to actual pop music. Wolf's new album Mud comes out next month, and we've already posted the singles " Twiggy " and " Bottle ." Today, she shares "I Won't Cry," a big, bruised old-school ballad with some country and some Southern rock in its DNA. It's got a big, melodramatic chorus, and she really sinks her teeth into it.

news.title: Apple Slab Pie
news.snippet: There’s almost nothing that signals fall to me like the smell of an apple pie baking in my kitchen. And when that’s happening there’s a high likelihood I’ll be gathering with friends and family in the near future because, well, pies are meant to be shared!While I love a traditional lattice-topped apple pie, I’ve found that a slab pie is the better, easier way to deliver classic apple pie flavors when you’re baking for a crowd.

news.title: Sebb’s, Glasgow G1: ‘A delicious bombardment of continents, cuisines and cultural trickledowns’ – restaurant review
news.snippet: Little bits of loveliness from Sauchiehall Street to the Silk Road, from a chef who wants to deliver maximum joy Sebb’s is a basement restaurant on Miller Street in Glasgow with a door that’s perilously easy to miss, even though it’s bright red. The first time I tried to find it, I waltzed past and almost ended up in the pants department of TK Maxx. I was luckier the second time around, and soon found myself descending a set of stairs into a room with the distinct vibe of a beatnik diner inside a bowling alley: there’s no natural light, there are booths that are perfect for conspiring in, a DJ playing psychedelic rock and food served in brown paper bags.
